verdicts.trueWording: "what seemed a simple joke ... entirely true and real"
verdicts.note: Wayback raw capture reached; quote exact. Essay's Gunnie/sailors passage: the play's Adam-and-Eve joke proves literal once Ushas' memory-wiped colonists are identified. All limbs on page.

verdicts.trueWording: "David felt that I should add one more paragraph saying"
verdicts.note: Quote exact in the block-quoted 'Secrets of the Greeks' extract, cited (Castle of Days, 416-17). The added paragraph is explanatory (sun fixed, happy ending) and concerns the Citadel of the Autarch ending. 'Editor' is the page's substance not its word: Hartwell is called TBOTNS's 'first reader', the man who would publish Citadel and later bought the coda.

verdicts.trueWording: "felt that a paragraph wasn't going to be enough"
verdicts.note: Quote exact, same block-quoted extract; Wolfe's clause answers Hartwell's one-paragraph proposal for the Citadel of the Autarch ending. Rejection polarity correct.

verdicts.trueWording: "the first book-length investigation of Wolfe's literary puzzlebox"
verdicts.note: Live Google Books record fetched with browser UA; quote exact in the publisher blurb that follows the iUniverse bibliographic line. Straight apostrophe on the page, matching the claim.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: the second limb — that a reviewer of the trade paperback counted 188 pages
verdicts.note: 204-page limb confirmed verbatim on the bibliographic line (claim's quote carries a stray space before the comma from HTML stripping; rendered page has 'iUniverse,'). The 188 figure is absent: the string '188' occurs nowhere on the page, and no reviewer or trade-paperback pagination is mentioned. That limb needs its own source.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that this is Borski's *second* collection — the page never numbers it
verdicts.trueWording: "from short stories to novellas to mega-book series"
verdicts.note: Range limb exact in the iUniverse blurb (claim drops 'mega-'). The page places the book as a successor only loosely — subtitle 'More Essays on the Fiction of Gene Wolfe' and 'once again literary detective Robert Borski' — and the word 'second' appears nowhere on the record. Ordinality must come from elsewhere.

verdicts.trueWording: "compiled by Michael Andre-Driussi with an introduction by Gene Wolfe"
verdicts.note: Cold Tonnage catalogue fetched live; quote exact in the Description block. 'First edition' limb carried by the Details block ('First edition (& 1st printing)', Sirius Fiction, San Francisco, 1994).
Quote exact, opening the Description block; the same entry gives first edition/1st printing and 1994, and distinguishes this printing from the 2008 updated reprint. All limbs on page.

verdicts.trueWording: "having recourse to invented terms; in no case have I done so"
verdicts.note: Live Wikipedia fetch; quote exact inside the block-quoted appendix extract in Language > Vocabulary, introduced as the appendix of The Shadow of the Torturer. Rendering limb carried by the same sentence's opening about rendering the book into English.

verdicts.trueWording: "replace yet undiscovered concepts by their closest twentieth-century equivalents"
verdicts.note: Quote exact, the sentence immediately following the invented-terms disclaimer in the same Language > Vocabulary block quote. Page reads 'I have been forced to replace ...', so 'replaced' is faithful.

verdicts.trueWording: "derived from a Latin word meaning \"without shadow\""
verdicts.note: Quote exact in Language > Vocabulary. Latitude limb carried by the same sentence's reason clause: the Ascians are tropic dwellers with no shadow at noon. The footnote on that sentence is Andre-Driussi, Lexicon Urthus (2nd ed., 2008), matching the claim's source attribution.

verdicts.trueWording: "a set of quotations from government propaganda called \"Correct Thought\""
verdicts.note: Quote exact in the 'Ascian language' section. 'Only' limb carried by the page's 'simply a set of quotations'; claim's 'state' for the page's 'government' is a synonym and the quote field keeps 'government'. Note the section adds that Ascians can still convey unintended meanings, which qualifies but does not contradict.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: restricting the cast to the Short Sun — the page's 'huge cast' spans both series
verdicts.trueWording: "dialects and accents spoken by the huge cast, all meticulously rendered"
verdicts.note: gwern mirror of the scifi.com column fetched live; quote exact, including 'the dozens of different dialects'. But the sentence heads a struggle-list opened by 'Both The Book of the Long Sun and The Book of the Short Sun', and the cast is glossed by 'everyone wants to talk to Silk' — so the praise covers the Long Sun and Short Sun books together, not the Short Sun cast alone. Safe rewording: the huge cast of the Long Sun and Short Sun books.

verdicts.trueWording: "refusal to unpack in easy terms a tale which is"
verdicts.note: Quote exact; the page's sentence continues past the quote to say the tale is inherently difficult to tell, so the claim's closing limb is on the page too. Attribution to Wolfe explicit ('Wolfe's refusal').

Quote exact, in the paragraph on Return to the Whorl's ending. 'Return' limb carried by the introducing clause about being reunited with much that had been thought lost; the three nouns are the concrete particulars listed after the colon.
